In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the motility of S. nemetoides is based on a modified glideosome machinery with the subpellicula microtubule system as the leading force-generating element.
the blastogregarines are the only apicomplexans exhibiting motility based on subpellicular cytoskeleton and not on glideosome.
S. nematoids are not able to perform gliding motility, but they are able to perform motility in the attached and detached state in a liquid environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glideosome concept does not apply to S. nematoids, but rather the subpellicula microtubules are the main motor structures in blastocyst formation and motility.
S. nematides motility is a result of a complex interaction between the subpellicula, the inner membrane complex and the actin-based cytoskeleton.
the motility of S. nem atoides is not based on a glideosome-like mechanism but on the actin-tubulin cross-linking complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glideosome concept is not applicable to the gregarines, which exhibit a variety of motility mechanisms.

the blastogregarines, despite their apicomplexan origin and the presence of the conserved glideosome machinery, evolved a novel mode of motility, probably due to the unique organisation of their cytoskeletal elements.
the motility mechanism in the S.  nematoides is based on the interaction of microtubules and actin, and that the glideosome is not the only mechanism responsible for the motility of Apicoplastida.
